# Final Plan: Documentation Access, Markdown Metadata, and Inbox Efficiency

> Origin: Generated by Planner via GPT on 2026-05-19. Human review: pending.

## Goal

Implement the first agentic documentation-access and Markdown-governance batch:

- Add metadata to all tracked Markdown files.
- Introduce a local, developer-provided documentation area under `docs/dev/`.
- Improve agent workflows so documentation lookup has a clear local-first hierarchy.
- Improve inbox consumption without replacing the Markdown inbox source of truth.

## Human Decisions Incorporated

- Use the Option A and Option B combination: local docs first, then human-granted external access through existing MCP/web retrieval surfaces.
- Use root `docs/` as the local documentation home, with a new untracked `docs/dev/` subtree for developer-provided stack documentation.
- Do not use Bitcraft product Documents/Knowledge for the agentic development stack in this iteration. Keep product runtime and AI development workflow ideologically separate.
- Use the metadata fields `created_at`, `edited_at`, `creator`, `editor`, and `ai_gen`.
- `ai_gen: true` is the default for agent-generated Markdown.
- `ai_gen: false` is the default for human-created Markdown.
- During document lifetime, only humans may change `ai_gen`.
- Use Vale as the only enforcement tool in this iteration. No extra scripts, hooks, CI gates, or product integrations.
- Apply metadata across all Markdown files, including Copilot customization files.
- Keep the first inbox improvement minimal because tracked inboxes currently add version-control noise but remain needed for backlog continuity.

## Compatibility Decision

The metadata change is approved for all Markdown files. The implementation must:

- Merge metadata into existing YAML frontmatter where frontmatter already exists.
- Add new YAML frontmatter where none exists.
- Preserve all existing Copilot customization frontmatter fields exactly unless a field value needs normal metadata date/editor updates.
- Validate prompt, agent, instruction, and skill loadability after edits through diagnostics, frontmatter review, and repository static checks.

This is compatible as a planned change because Markdown frontmatter is already used across Copilot customizations and the requested fields are plain YAML scalar fields. The remaining risk is client-specific strict-schema behavior, so validation is mandatory after implementation.

## Documentation Access Model

### Local Documentation Root

Add `docs/dev/` as a developer-local documentation root. It is not tracked by Git and is populated by developers or humans with local documentation packs.

`.gitignore` must ignore:

```gitignore
docs/dev/
```

Because ignored empty directories cannot be versioned, repository-tracked documentation should describe the convention outside `docs/dev/`, for example in `docs/agentic-ai.md` and `.github/agentic-ai/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md`.

### Documentation Stack Layout

Each local documentation stack should use this folder shape:

```text
docs/dev/<stack-slug>/
  STACK.md
  sources/
    <human-provided files>
```

`STACK.md` is an AI-allowed management document generated by AI Ops unless a human changes it. It should use Markdown plus YAML frontmatter because that keeps the stack readable to humans and parseable by agents/MCP.

Recommended `STACK.md` frontmatter:

```yaml
---
created_at: 2026-05-19
edited_at: 2026-05-19
creator: ai-ops
editor: ai-ops
ai_gen: true
name: GitHub Copilot Documentation
description: Local documentation stack for Copilot agentic development guidance.
sources_required: true
sources:
  - path: sources/example.md
    kind: local-file
    provided_by: human
external_sources:
  - url: https://example.invalid/docs
    kind: official-docs
validation_status: pending
---
```

Only the first five fields are part of the global Markdown metadata standard. The remaining fields are stack-management fields for `docs/dev/<stack-slug>/STACK.md`.

### Documentation Lookup Hierarchy

Normal agent workflow:

1. Attempt to find relevant local docs in `docs/dev/` and repository governance docs.
2. If the human explicitly grants documentation access, attempt approved external source retrieval.
3. If external source retrieval is insufficient and the human requested broader research, use web search/retrieval and collect sources.
4. Delegate to the human when sources are absent, conflicting, inaccessible, or require approval.

Deep research workflow:

- Steps 1 through 3 are all expected to run when available.
- The researcher must report local/remote source discrepancies instead of silently preferring one.
- If local docs are stale or source validation is missing, the output must say so.

Local/remote discrepancy workflow:

- Compare local `docs/dev/<stack-slug>/sources/` files with approved remote sources from `STACK.md` when the human requests documentation validation.
- Report additions, removals, version/date mismatch, and unresolved conflicts.
- Do not auto-update local docs unless explicitly asked; human-provided source files remain human-controlled inputs.

## Metadata Standard

Global Markdown metadata fields:

```yaml
---
created_at: 2026-05-19
edited_at: 2026-05-19
creator: human | <agent-slug>
editor: human | <agent-slug>
ai_gen: true | false
---
```

Rules:

- Every tracked Markdown file must include the fields.
- `ai_gen: true` is the default for documents created by agents.
- `ai_gen: false` is the default for documents created by humans.
- Only humans may change `ai_gen` after creation.
- Agents may update `edited_at` and `editor` when they edit an `ai_gen: true` document or when the human explicitly permits editing a human-created document.
- Agents must not change `created_at` after the field is introduced, except while adding initial metadata in the implementation batch.
- `creator` and `editor` should use `human` or the Bitcraft agent slug, for example `planner`, `researcher`, `ai-ops`, or `lead-dev`.

Initial backfill rule:

- Existing files should receive `created_at: 2026-05-19` and `edited_at: 2026-05-19` unless there is reliable existing file provenance in the file itself.
- Existing AI-generated standalone reports may use `creator` matching the provenance line when obvious; otherwise use `creator: human` for pre-existing repo docs and `editor: planner` or the implementing agent for the backfill.
- Existing files that are clearly agent-generated or agentic operational artifacts should generally use `ai_gen: true`; stable human-facing project docs should use `ai_gen: false` unless the human directs otherwise.

## Inbox Improvements

Round 1 keeps the inbox model simple:

- Keep `.github/inboxes/<agent-slug>/inbox.md` as the tracked backlog source for continuity.
- Avoid migrating inboxes to Jira, SQLite, JSON, or YAML in this batch.
- Keep completed items removed promptly to reduce version-control noise.
- Add or update guidance so agents prefer concise inbox items and avoid using inboxes as logs.
- If implementation capacity allows, add an additive `read_inbox_structured(agent_slug)` MCP tool that parses existing Markdown into structured fields. Do not change existing `read_inbox(agent_slug)` behavior.

If the inbox continues to clog version control after this batch, a future phase can evaluate untracked local inboxes, Jira/Bitbucket-backed work items, or a generated snapshot model.

## Technical Requirements

### `.gitignore`

- Add `docs/dev/` with a comment explaining it is developer-local documentation loaded by humans/developers.
- Do not ignore the rest of `docs/`.
- Do not change `.github/inboxes` tracking in this batch.

### MCP And Documentation Access

- Update `mcp-server/server.py` to tolerate missing `docs/dev/` if adding documentation-stack discovery.
- If stack discovery is implemented, expose read-only tools only, such as `list_doc_stacks()` and `read_doc_stack(stack_slug)`.
- Returned stack data must include source paths and validation status without free-form path access.
- Update `mcp-server/README.md` and `.github/mcp/bitcraft-mcp-spec.md` if any MCP tools are added.
- No write-capable MCP tools.

### Governance And Agent Guidance

- Update `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/agentic-ai/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md`, and `docs/agentic-ai.md` with:
  - metadata rule,
  - human-only `ai_gen` modification rule,
  - local-first documentation lookup hierarchy,
  - deep research discrepancy reporting,
  - `docs/dev/` local stack convention,
  - inbox hygiene expectations.

### Vale Enforcement

- Add or update Vale rules under `.github/vale/styles/Bitcraft/` to flag Markdown missing the five metadata fields.
- Keep enforcement to Vale only in this iteration.
- Vale checks can focus on required field presence and simple `ai_gen: true|false` shape.
- Do not add custom scripts, hooks, or CI enforcement in this batch.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Metadata

- Every tracked Markdown file has exactly one YAML frontmatter block containing `created_at`, `edited_at`, `creator`, `editor`, and `ai_gen`.
- Files that already had YAML frontmatter preserve required Copilot fields.
- `ai_gen` defaults follow creator source: agent-generated documents default true; human-created documents default false.
- Agent guidance states only humans may change `ai_gen` after creation.

### Documentation Access

- `docs/dev/` is ignored by Git and documented as developer-local.
- Local documentation stack layout and `STACK.md` metadata are documented.
- Agent workflow has a clear fallback hierarchy: local docs, explicit external source retrieval, web retrieval for deep research, human delegation.
- Deep research guidance requires local/remote discrepancy reporting.
- Product Documents/Knowledge ingestion is explicitly out of scope.

### Inbox Efficiency

- Inbox guidance is tightened to reduce version-control noise.
- Existing inbox files remain tracked and usable.
- Existing `read_inbox(agent_slug)` MCP behavior is not broken.
- Any structured inbox MCP enhancement is additive.

### Validation

- Markdown diagnostics show no new errors on changed files.
- `npx markdownlint-cli2 --config .markdownlint.jsonc ".github/**/*.md" "docs/**/*.md" "*.md"` passes or known pre-existing warnings are documented.
- `vale --config .vale.ini .github docs *.md` passes or only reports accepted pre-existing suggestions.
- If MCP tools are changed, a focused smoke test confirms the server starts and the changed tools return safe read-only data.
- Copilot customization files are reviewed after metadata insertion to ensure existing required frontmatter fields remain present.
